classification.habit: Small to medium evergreen or semi-evergreen tree
classification.habitat: Moist forests, hills and subtropical woodland

identification.description: Tree with simple leaves, pale flowers and ovoid fruits; stem bark is the principal crude drug.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium tree with a spreading crown.
identification.stem: Woody trunk and branches with grey-brown bark.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, elliptic to oblong leaves with entire or finely serrulate margins.
identification.flower: Small pale flowers, often in axillary or terminal clusters.
identification.fruit: Small ovoid drupe, becoming coloured as it matures.
identification.seed: Single to few seeds enclosed in the fruit.
identification.bark: Grey-brown stem bark; medicinal crude drug commonly consists of bark pieces.

therapeutics.precautions: Clinical use requires authenticated crude drug and appropriate professional guidance.

major_constituents: Tannins and phenolic constituents have been reported

modern_information.evidence_summary: Lodhra is a traditional bark drug studied for astringent and other biological properties; clinical claims require evidence-specific interpretation.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use authenticated Symplocos racemosa material; avoid assuming similarly named species are equivalent.

viva_questions: What is the botanical name of Lodhra?
mnemonics: Lodhra = bark drug with Kashaya profile
student.quick_revision: Lodhra—Symplocos racemosa; Symplocaceae; stem bark; Kashaya, Laghu-Ruksha, Sheeta.

teaching_points: Demonstrate authenticated bark and whole plant morphology.
discussion_points: Discuss bark-drug identification and adulteration risk.
Relate Kashaya properties to traditional uses.
practical_points: Observe bark colour, texture and leaf morphology.

doctor.quick_reference: Traditional Lodhra profile centers on stem bark and astringent/gynaecological contexts.
key_precautions: Authenticate the bark before medicinal use.
